questions.q: What is a journal line type?
options: A custom script written by a consultant for every transaction
A seeded definition of a kind of accounting line, such as Invoice, Tax, or Freight, with debit/credit and accounting-class properties already set
The final GL account posted to
A report that lists subledger journal entries
questions.explain: Journal line types are seeded by Oracle to represent kinds of lines, and consultants build logic on top of them rather than creating new ones from scratch.

questions.q: What does a journal line rule add on top of a journal line type?
options: A new Chart of Accounts
The specific conditions under which that kind of line should actually generate on a journal entry
A replacement for the General Ledger
A supplier bank account number
questions.explain: Journal line rules attach real logic and conditions to a journal line type, controlling exactly when that line should appear.

questions.q: In the worked example, why didn't every invoice generate a Tax journal line?
options: Tax lines are generated randomly
Because the Tax journal line rule is typically conditioned to fire only when the invoice has a non-zero tax amount
Tax lines are never generated by Subledger Accounting
Because freight and tax always cancel each other out
questions.explain: Journal line rules can include conditions, such as firing only when tax is present on the invoice; invoices with no tax don't satisfy that condition.

questions.q: What is the purpose of merging lines that would post to the same account?
options: To intentionally make the journal entry unbalanced
To delete transaction history
To keep the journal entry readable instead of listing many separate lines that all hit the same account
To avoid using accounting classes
questions.explain: Merging combines lines heading to the same account into one line, which keeps journal entries from becoming cluttered.

questions.q: What is an accounting class used for, as described in this lesson?
options: It has no practical use and is purely cosmetic
It determines a supplier's payment terms
It groups related journal line types (like all Invoice lines or all Tax lines) so reports can label and organize journal lines meaningfully
It replaces the need for journal line rules
questions.explain: The accounting class assigned to a journal line rule is used by downstream reporting, such as the Account Analysis Report, to group and label lines.
